summary: Thomas Blom Hansen works in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at Aalborg University (MSc 2013-2018) and held posts at Edinburgh (~1999-2003), Amsterdam (~2003-2010), Yale (~2007-2008), Stanford (Professor, 2010), and the University of Natal.

Thomas Bond Lindsay was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Wesleyan University (M.A. ~1870-1874) and Boston University (Ph.D. by 1882). He taught at Newton High School (1877-1888) and Boston University (1878-1909).

Thomas Borchert is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the University of Chicago under Bruce Lincoln and others, and he became an Associate Professor of Religion at the University of Vermont (attested 2017).

Thomas Bruce Ridgeway worked in computational linguistics and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Washington by 1986 and served as Director of its Center for Computing and Humanities until 1994.

Thomas Burrow was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Cambridge under Edward James Rapson. He held posts at the British Museum, SOAS, and Oxford, where he was Boden Professor of Sanskrit from 1944 to 1976.

Thomas Callan Hodson, a linguist and Indologist, studied at The Queen's College, Oxford. He served as Registrar at Queen Mary University of London (1903-1914) and Reader of Ethnography at the University of Cambridge (1926-1937).

Thomas Candy was a scholar in linguistics and Indology who studied at Magdalen College School. He served as Superintendent (1837) and Principal (1851-1857) at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute.

Thomas Chalmers, working in religious studies, was educated at the University of St Andrews and the University of Edinburgh. He later held posts at the University of St Andrews (~1823-1828) and the University of Edinburgh (~1828-1843).

Thomas Christian Tychsen was a linguist and historian. After studying under Christian Gottlob Heyne at Göttingen, he became Professor of Theology (1785) and Professor of Philosophy (1788) at the University of Göttingen.

Thomas Cleary worked in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and philosophy. He studied under E. Bruce Brooks, earned a Ph.D. from Harvard University, and obtained a JD from the University of California, Berkeley.
Thomas Craven was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He completed an M.A. at Northwestern University and a B.D. at Garrett-Evangelical Theological Seminary.

Thomas Doctor works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling and the University of Lausanne, supervised by Tom Tillemans and others, and held a post at Rangjung Yeshe Institute.

Thomas E. Crow is an art historian who studied at Pomona College and UCLA. He directed the Getty Research Institute (2000-2007) and became Rosalie Solow Professor of Modern Art at New York University in 2007.

Thomas Edward Colebrooke worked in Indology and history/archaeology, studying under Jagannatha, at Eton College, and at East India Company College. He served as President (1864-1882) and Vice-President (until 1890) of the Royal Asiatic Society.

Thomas Erskine Perry, an Indology and history scholar, studied at Trinity College, Cambridge and the University of Munich. He served as a Judge on Bombay's Supreme Court of Judicature (1841-1852) and member of the Council of India (1859-1882).

Thomas Ethelbert Page was a scholar in linguistics and history/archaeology. He studied at Shrewsbury School and St John's College (~1869-1873), and later held a post at Charterhouse School from 1899 to 1936.

Thomas Freeman Yarnall works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at Columbia University under Robert A. F. Thurman by 2003 and later served there as Executive Editor (attested 2007).

Thomas Fulton Cummings, a linguist and Indologist, studied at Westminster College and Union Theological Seminary. He taught at Jhelum Theological Seminary, Biblical Seminary in New York (1912), Union Theological Seminary (1918-1920), and Drew University (1918-1933).

Thomas George Percival Spear was an Indologist and historian who earned his Ph.D. at St Catharine's College, Cambridge. He taught at St. Stephen's College, Delhi (1924-1940) and lectured in South Asian History at Cambridge (~1963-1969).

Thomas Grahame Bailey was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He earned a D.Litt. from the University of Edinburgh by 1920 and served as Reader in Hindustani at SOAS University of London (~1920-1940).
